correctness.rationale: Deleting i removes its incoming and outgoing internal weights and leaves i as the sole outsider; summation of the resulting core upper bounds gives αW≤(3α−1)W. For W>0 this rules out every α<1/2. At equality, all bounds are tight, and D/2 is feasible since the minimum incoming sum is bounded by the incoming cut sum. Above the threshold the included positive scaling of the edge-splitting zonotope has affine direction space spanned by positive-edge endpoint differences, of rank n−c, including isolates. Opposite sides of each positive-support component cut have external worth zero even if listed zero arcs cross it, so each component sum is fixed. The argument does not require arbitrary coalitional values to be additive across those components. For a restriction to S and T⊆S, if there are exterior incoming arcs from N∖S the minimum for T is at most the exterior minimum for S; otherwise it is at most the incoming sum from S∖T. This verifies the proposed restricted allocations with the original coalition values. If W=0 the singleton constraints and zero total force the zero allocation for all α. An independent two-vertex unit-arc calculation gives x₁∈[0,2α−1], reproducing the threshold and dimension on that instance only. The uploaded verifier was inspected, not run; the 2,555 reported rational cases are supplementary, not an independent audit or universal proof.
